rows.claim: God's response both condemns moral degradation and reassures believers that God sees their humiliation, hates it, and punishes it, raising their spirits above hostile plots.
rows.anchor: الله يرى ما يقع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan surah has five verses and recalls a famous pre-Islamic Arabian event that displays God's care for the sacred precinct selected as the cradle of the new faith.
rows.anchor: حادث مستفيض الشهرة في حياة الجزيرة العربية قبل البعثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe Abraha, the Abyssinian ruler of Yemen after Abyssinian rule replaced Persian rule, building a magnificent church for Ethiopia's king to divert Arabs from Mecca's sanctuary.
rows.anchor: كان قد بنى كنيسة في اليمن باسم ملك الحبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs remained attached to the Kaaba as the house of Abraham and Ishmael and took pride in that ancestry; they regarded their own beliefs as better than those of nearby People of the Book.
rows.anchor: كانوا يعتقدون أنهم أبناء إبراهيم وإسماعيل صاحبي هذا البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraha then resolved to demolish the Kaaba with a large army and elephants, led by a particularly famous elephant.
rows.anchor: وفي مقدمتها فيل عظيم ذو شهرة خاصة عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu Nafr, a Yemeni notable and ruler, rallied his people and other responding Arabs to defend the sanctuary, but Abraha defeated and captured him.
rows.anchor: رجل من أشراف أهل اليمن وملوكهم يقال له ذو نفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khath'ami and two Arab tribes, joined by many others, were defeated and Nufayl was captured; he accepted the role of guide through Arab territory.
rows.anchor: نفيل ابن حبيب الخثعمي في قبيلتين من العرب ومعهما عرب كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Taif, Thaqif men redirected Abraha toward Mecca to protect their own shrine to al-Lat, and supplied him a guide to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: البيت الذي يقصده ليس عندهم إنما هو في مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At al-Mughammis Abraha sent a commander to raid Tihama; the seized property included two hundred camels belonging to Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, Quraysh's leading elder.
rows.anchor: فأصاب فيها مائتي بعير لعبد المطلب بن هاشم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh, Kinana, Hudhayl, and others considered fighting but withdrew after recognizing they could not match Abraha's force.
rows.anchor: عرفوا أنهم لا طاقة لهم به فتركوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraha's envoy said the king came to destroy the sanctuary, not to fight Meccans, and would spare their lives if they did not resist; he summoned the city's leader.
rows.anchor: الملك لم يأت لحربهم وإنما جاء لهدم هذا البيت

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: Abd al-Muttalib said he had no capacity to fight and left the sanctuary to its divine owner: if God wished, He would protect His house and Abraham's sanctuary.
rows.anchor: عبد المطلب فيما جاء به قال له : والله ما نريد حربه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Abd al-Muttalib was exceptionally handsome, imposing, and distinguished; Abraha honored him but avoided seating him on the royal throne before the Abyssinians.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : وكان عبد المطلب أوسم الناس وأجملهم وأعظمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abraha asked his need, Abd al-Muttalib requested only the return of his two hundred camels, prompting Abraha to rebuke him for neglecting the threatened sanctuary.
rows.anchor: حاجتي أن يرد علي الملك مائتي بعير أصابها لي

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: Abd al-Muttalib answered that he owned the camels while the House had a Lord who would protect it; Abraha denied that protection, then returned the camels.
rows.anchor: عبد المطلب : إني أنا رب الإبل . وإن للبيت رب سيمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd al-Muttalib told Quraysh to leave Mecca for mountain heights, then prayed at the Kaaba's door-ring with other Quraysh men seeking God's help.
rows.anchor: ثم انصرف عبد المطلب إلى قريش فأخبرهم الخبر ،  وأمرهم بالخروج من مكة

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: A report attributes to Abd al-Muttalib a prayer-poem asking God to protect His sanctuary as people protect their belongings and to frustrate the invaders' cross and schemes.
rows.anchor: روي عن عبد المطلب أنه أنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elephant knelt and would not enter Mecca, and efforts to make it advance failed.
rows.anchor: فبرك الفيل دون مكة لا يدخلها

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya the Prophet said his she-camel had not become recalcitrant; the same restrainer who stopped the Elephant had held her back.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ]  "  ما خلأت القصواء ،  وما ذاك لها بخلق

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections has the Prophet say God restrained the elephant and then empowered His Messenger and the believers; Qutb treats these reports as confirming the event.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] قال يوم فتح مكة :  "  إن الله حبس عن مكة الفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army was destroyed by flocks of birds pelting it with stones; accounts say Abraha was injured, lost flesh bit by bit on the journey to Sanaa, and died after his chest split open.
rows.anchor: وأصيب أبرهة في جسده ، وخرجوا به معهم يسقط أنملة أنملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports disagree about the birds' kind and size, and about the stones' size, nature, and effect; some also report that smallpox and measles appeared in Mecca that year.
rows.anchor: تختلف الروايات هنا في تحديد نوع هذه الجماعات من الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who restrict miracles and favor familiar natural laws see a smallpox or measles epidemic as the closer explanation and identify the birds with disease-carrying flies or mosquitoes.
rows.anchor: يرى الذين يميلون إلى تضييق نطاق الخوارق والغيبيات

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: The quoted account by Muhammad Abduh says smallpox or measles spread through the army of Abraha the next day.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ الإمام الشيخ محمد عبده في تفسيره للسورة في جزء عم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the explanation quoted from Abduh, birds may be mosquitoes or flies carrying germs from poisonous clay, causing sores and flesh decay.
rows.anchor: فيجوز لك أن تعتقد أن هذا الطير من جنس البعوض أو الذباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation quoted from Abduh says small creatures and microbes are troops belonging to God, so the event needs no gigantic or exotic birds.
rows.anchor: ولا يتوقف ظهور أثر قدرة الله تعالى في قهر الطاغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh says accounts beyond his disease explanation should not be accepted without reinterpretation, even if their transmission is sound.
rows.anchor: وما عدا ذلك فهو مما لا يصح قبوله إلا بتأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb rejects treating either Abduh's contaminated-clay disease model or reports of stones piercing bodies as the uniquely preferable explanation: both are possible and neither better displays God's power.
rows.anchor: لا نرى أن هذه الصورة أو تلك أدل على قدرة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's familiar and unfamiliar patterns are both divine sunnah; what people call a miracle is extraordinary only relative to their limited experience, and ordinary sunrise or childbirth is wondrous too.
rows.anchor: إن سنة الله ليست فقط هي ما عهده البشر وما عرفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb accepts a miracle when reports are sound or the text and circumstances indicate it, and does not require familiar natural causes to explain every event.
rows.anchor: لا نقف أمام الخارقة مترددين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For this event Qutb leans toward an unfamiliar supernatural episode, while rejecting sensational reports about the birds' exact sizes, shapes, and colors as likely exaggerated.
rows.anchor: لا نقف أمام الخارقة مترددين ولا مؤولين لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb's preference rests on the House's divinely planned role as a safe gathering place for the new faith and the need for its cradle to be free from outside political control.
rows.anchor: كان يريد أن يحفظه ليكون مثابة للناس وأمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event was meant to remain an unmistakable sign for generations and a post-prophetic reminder to Quraysh of God's protection and zeal for sacred things.
rows.anchor: ويجعل هذا الحادث عبرة ظاهرة مكشوفة لجميع الأنظار في جميع الأجيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb says common measles or smallpox does not explain flesh falling away limb by limb or the chest splitting; the Qur'anic image directly suggests the army was like eaten foliage.
rows.anchor: الجدري أو الحصبة لا يسقط الجسم عضوا عضوا وأنملة أنملة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima's statement only says smallpox first appeared in Arabia that year; it does not say Abraha's army contracted it.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة : وهو أول جدري ظهر ببلاد العرب

rows.speaker: يعقوب بن عتبة
rows.claim: Yaqub ibn Utba's report likewise says measles and smallpox were first seen in Arabia that year, without specifically identifying Abraha's army as the victims.
rows.anchor: وقال يعقوب بن عتبة فيما حدث : إن أول ما رؤيت الحصبة والجدري ببلاد العرب ذلك العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If only the army was targeted while nearby Arabs were spared, selective infection would itself be extraordinary; familiarity is no reason to force that particular explanation.
rows.anchor: عدم إصابة العرب القريبين بمثله في حينه تبدو خارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb understands the rationalist school's caution as a response to superstition, Isra'iliyyat, and modern scientific skepticism, and credits its effort to restore religious credibility and attend to regular natural laws.
rows.anchor: محمد عبده - كما شاع في تفسير تلميذيه الأستاذ الشيخ رشيد رضا والأستاذ الشيخ عبد القادر المغربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He nevertheless criticizes Abduh's school and pupils Rashid Rida and Abd al-Qadir al-Maghribi for overcorrecting, making familiar natural processes the only rule and allegorizing unseen events to fit reason.
rows.anchor: محمد عبده - كما شاع في تفسير تلميذيه الأستاذ الشيخ رشيد رضا والأستاذ الشيخ عبد القادر المغربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb's rule is to receive premises and reasoning from clear Qur'anic statements, rather than judge them by prior human conclusions limited by experience; this need not mean yielding to superstition.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن نواجه هذه النصوص لنتلقى منها مقرراتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question is meant to evoke wonder at an event Arabs already knew and used as a dating era; the Prophet's birth was popularly placed in that same year, a providential coincidence.
rows.anchor: حتى لقد جعلوه مبدأ تاريخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah does not teach an unknown story; it reminds its audience of a familiar event to direct them toward its deeper significance.
rows.anchor: إنما كانت تذكيرا بأمر يعرفونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question says God frustrated Abraha's plot so it missed its destination; it reminds Quraysh that God protected the House when they were powerless, rebukes their ingratitude, and warns their present strength cannot defeat Muhammad and the believers.
rows.anchor: أي ألم يضل مكرهم فلا يبلغ هدفه وغايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's response is pictured as sending birds in abābīl, meaning flocks or successive groups, to attack the army.
rows.anchor: والأبابيل : الجماعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjīl is a Persian compound whose two elements mean stone and clay, hence stones stained or coated with clay.
rows.anchor: وسجيل كلمة فارسية مركبة من كلمتين تفيدان : حجر وطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṣf is dry foliage; eaten foliage is crushed into crumbs, whether chewed by insects or ground by an animal, portraying bodily disintegration from the stones.
rows.anchor: والعصف : الجاف من ورق الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb says there is no need to reinterpret the image as destruction by smallpox or measles.
rows.anchor: ولا ضرورة لتأويلها بأنها تصوير لحال هلاكهم بمرض الجدري أو الحصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not entrust the sanctuary's protection to the polytheists: He let them be defeated so they would not claim credit, then intervened openly to proclaim His protection.
rows.anchor: لم يرد أن يكل حماية بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This intervention should have led Quraysh and the Arabs to accept Islam when the Messenger came, rather than let pride in sanctuary service and idolatry block them; the reminder rebukes their stubbornness.
rows.anchor: أن تبادر قريش ويبادر العرب إلى الدخول في دين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God kept the sanctuary and holy land beyond the control of the People of the Book despite its pagan custodians, preserving it as a free cradle for the coming faith.
rows.anchor: أن يحطموا البيت الحرام أو يسيطروا على الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb applies the lesson to his own era, expressing hope that God will protect the sacred sites and Medina from international Crusader and Zionist designs.
rows.anchor: الصليبية العالمية والصهيونية العالمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Islam the Arabs lacked political weight: Yemen was under Persian or Abyssinian power, the north under Rome, and central Arabia remained divided or pastoral; the Elephant year showed their weakness against foreign invasion.
rows.anchor: بل لم يكن لهم كيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs gained an international role by identifying as Muslims and following Islam alone, rather than elevating ethnic or tribal chauvinism.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أنهم ومسلمون . مسلمون فقط

rows.speaker: ربعي بن عامر
rows.claim: At Yazdegerd's court, the Muslim envoy summarized the mission as freeing people from worship of people to worship of God, from worldly constriction to the Hereafter's breadth, and from oppressive religions to Islam's justice.
rows.anchor: كما قال ربعي بن عامر رسول المسلمين في مجلس يزدجرد :  " الله ابتعثنا لنخرج الناس من عبادة العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab strength and leadership endured while they upheld Islam; when they returned to ethnic and tribal banners, other nations subdued them because they abandoned God and He left them.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا انحرفوا عنها وذكروا عنصريتهم وعصبيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb argues that without Islam the Arabs have no distinctive idea to offer humanity or historic role; like the Tatars and western barbarians, conquerors without a guiding idea are absorbed by the peoples they conquer.
rows.anchor: والأمم التي لم تكن تمثل فكرة كالتتار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's lesson urges Arabs to remember that their life, strength, and leadership depend on carrying Islam.
rows.anchor: وهذا ما يجب أن يذكره العرب جيدا إذا هم أرادوا الحياة
